study_identification.title: Revealing Individual Neuroanatomical Heterogeneity in Alzheimer Disease Using Neuroanatomical Normative Modeling

study_characteristics.study_objective: Apply neuroanatomical normative modeling of cortical thickness to characterize individual-level heterogeneity and outliers in AD, MCI, and controls, relate heterogeneity to cognition and CSF biomarkers, and test whether heterogeneity predicts conversion from MCI to AD.

deviation_metric.answer: Regional Z-scores (per region); outlier threshold Z < -1.96; Total Outlier Count (tOC) across 148 regions; mean cortical thickness Z-score

deviation_metric.supporting_text: "Z-scores per region were calculated, resulting in a Z-score brain map per participant. Regions with Z-scores < -1.96 were classified as outliers."; group comparisons reference tOC.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Linear regressions (adjusted for age/sex) linking total outlier count (tOC) to memory and executive function (both p=2.2e-16); associations with CSF Aβ (β=0.002, p=0.022) and p-tau (β=0.1301, p=1.04e-8). Survival analysis (Cox proportional hazards) in 454 MCI showed higher tOC increased risk of conversion to AD within 3 years (HR=1.028 per 1 tOC; ~31.4% per +10 tOC).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Individualized cortical thickness z-score maps reveal heterogeneous regional atrophy in AD; higher total outlier burden relates to poorer cognition, adverse CSF biomarkers, and greater risk of MCI→AD conversion.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: AD patients had a median of 12 outlier regions (of 148), with the left parahippocampal gyrus showing the highest outlier proportion (47%). Group differences in outlier burden were significant (ANOVA F(2,1022)=95.39, p=2.0×10^-16), with AD> MCI> controls. Within-group dissimilarity (Hamming distance) was greatest in AD (ANOVA F(2,1024)=209.42, p=2.2×10^-16). tOC was associated with memory (β=-0.01, p=2.2×10^-16) and executive function (β=-0.02, p=2.2×10^-16), and with CSF Aβ (β=0.002, p=0.022) and p-tau (β=0.1301, p=1.04×10^-8). In 454 MCI with follow-up, higher tOC predicted increased conversion risk to AD over 3 years (HR=1.028 [95% CI 1.016–1.039], p=1.8×10^-16; ~31.4% per +10 tOC).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Clinical dataset (ADNI) underrepresents cognitive domains beyond memory/executive/language; other potential limitations (e.g., broader external validation, detailed demographic summaries) are not detailed in the provided text.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: Normative modeling implemented with PCNtoolkit v0.20, using HBR for site effects and transfer learning to calibrate to ADNI (70% site-stratified controls). Scripts available on GitHub; approach highlights individualized markers potentially useful for stratification and prognosis.

general_notes.general_notes: ADNI clinical MRI from 62 sites; total ADNI sample n=1,492, with 70% controls reserved for calibration and 1,027 used for analysis; reference cohort aggregated across ~60 sites (n=33,072). Statistical scripts: github.com/serenaverdi/ADNI_normative-modelling. PCNtoolkit repo: github.com/amarquand/PCNtoolkit. Controls count (n=159) noted in text; demographics table referenced but not embedded.
